clue.text: Plant employees' outer clothing protected by uniform

indicators.note: the uniform word wraps around the pair of letters, as a guard surrounds what it protects

parts.note: uniform things are all the same

indicators.note: the clothing of a word is its outside, so only the first and last letters of employees' are used

explanation.surface: Staff at a factory have their overalls covered by a company uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a factory, which 'employees' supports, but it is a herb grown for its seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: A herb cultivated for its oily seeds, so it is a kind of plant.

clue.text: Screws up protecting small business? No-one's a winner with this

indicators.note: the reversed word goes around the business letters, guarding them
in a down answer up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: screws is slang for prison warders
Co is the short form of company, a business

explanation.surface: Someone botches a deal protecting a small firm, so nobody wins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screws up' looks like a verb meaning botches; it is warders read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A football match ending level with goals on both sides means neither team takes victory.

clue.text: Good number beginning to faint in science fiction film, perhaps

indicators.note: in places these pieces inside the science fiction letters

parts.note: pi is short for pious, good

indicators.note: beginning to points to the first letter of faint

explanation.surface: A well-loved scene where someone starts to faint in a science fiction movie.
explanation.definitionFit: A follow-up derived from an earlier work, as a film can be.

clue.text: Woman heading off big game, stampeding

indicators.note: stampeding animals run in disorder, so the letters are mixed up
heading off means the first letter of big is removed

explanation.surface: A woman heads off a herd of big game as it stampedes.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, the familiar form of Margaret.

clue.text: Variety of tips welcomed by female follower of fashion

indicators.note: the female word takes the shuffled letters in, as a host welcomes a guest

parts.note: her is the female pronoun

indicators.note: a variety of the letters means some new arrangement of them

explanation.surface: A woman with style picks up a range of tips on what to wear.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who keeps up with the latest trends, often self-consciously, is a trendy fashion follower.

clue.text: Accommodation no longer available to rent? That's a pity, on reflection

indicators.note: reflection reverses an image, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a property that has been let is no longer free to rent
oh is a sigh of regret

explanation.surface: A sad notice that the flat is no longer available, with a sigh of regret.
explanation.definitionFit: A place offering rooms to guests for the night is a type of accommodation.

clue.text: Advocate not supporting single European currency?

parts.note: pro means supporting
the pound is a currency in Europe

explanation.surface: An advocate who opposes the single European currency, the euro.
explanation.walkthrough: Someone against the euro is in favour of keeping the British pound; the question mark flags that whimsical reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To put forward an idea for consideration is to argue for it.

clue.text: Old silver coin collection rejected as well: new

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the collection word is read backwards

parts.note: a set is a collection
too means as well

explanation.surface: A collector's set of old silver coins is rejected, and a new one too.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic coin of silver, a shilling-type piece from 16th-century France and Italy.

clue.text: Stove with burners — all a stockist has

definitions.meaning: a cooking stove with hotplates and an oven
the full selection of goods a shop carries

explanation.surface: A shop's complete stock of cookers with burners.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a kitchen cooker and the full assortment of products a retailer offers.

clue.text: £5 I've spent on line? That's the limit

indicators.note: spent means used up and gone, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a fiver is a five-pound note
a tier is a row or line, as of seats

explanation.surface: Someone has blown a five-pound note on a bet and declares that the last straw.
explanation.definitionFit: A border marking the edge of a territory or field is its outermost boundary.

clue.text: Outstanding all-rounder finally eliminated from water sport

indicators.note: the chosen letter is knocked out of the sport, as a player is eliminated from a contest

parts.note: rowing is a sport practised on water

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of all-rounder

explanation.surface: A star all-rounder is finally knocked out of a rowing event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' looks like praise for the all-rounder; it means a debt still unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: Money still unpaid is outstanding, the same as being still due.

clue.text: Special operations winkling out European killer

indicators.note: special here is read as specially arranged, signalling a reshuffle of the letters
winkling out means extracting, so a letter is taken from the pool before rearranging

explanation.surface: Special forces carry out an operation to remove a European assassin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special' is the anagram signal and 'winkling out' removes E from OPERATIONS before the remaining nine letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A poison laid for rodents is literally something that kills.

clue.text: Affecting circulation of the French best seller?

indicators.note: circulation means going round, so the pieces are turned to read backwards

parts.note: la is a French word for the
a best seller is a number one book, NO 1 and a tome, with the 1 as the letter I

explanation.surface: A newspaper's circulation figures for a French best seller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'best seller' gives NO 1 TOME, the 1 read as I; 'circulation of' turns LA NOI TOME round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something moving that stirs the feelings is affecting, a close synonym.

clue.text: Sea air I discovered east of Australia

indicators.note: in an across answer east is to the right, so the I word comes after the Australia word

parts.note: Oz is the familiar name for Australia
I as the Roman numeral is one

explanation.surface: Someone finds the bracing sea breeze of the Pacific coast east of Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh seaside air is popularly said to be full of this gas, a seaside idiom.

clue.text: Meaning to dismiss Head, causing disagreement

indicators.note: dismissing the head means dropping the first letter

parts.note: the drift of an argument is its meaning

explanation.surface: Plans to sack the headteacher cause a row in the staffroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a headteacher being sacked; it is the first letter of DRIFT.
explanation.definitionFit: A split or breach between people who have fallen out is a disagreement.

clue.text: Lack of harmony is issue in waltz, say

indicators.note: in says the first pieces sit inside the waltz word

parts.note: a waltz is an example of a dance
a son is a man's issue, his offspring

explanation.surface: The band's playing is out of tune during a waltz.
explanation.definitionFit: Discord in music or relationships, a clash of sounds, is the absence of harmony.

clue.text: Fielder finished top

parts.note: slip is a cricket fielding position next to the wicketkeeper
something finished is over

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder is done for the day.
explanation.walkthrough: Slip is a cricket position beside the wicketkeeper; 'top' is a garment, not the summit.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeveless pullover is a garment worn on the upper body.

clue.text: Old weapon put in cold storage for life

parts.note: ex means former, old

indicators.note: put in places the weapon inside the cold storage word

parts.note: ice keeps food cold
the Sten is a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: An outdated weapon is put in cold storage for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for life' suggests a sentence; the Sten is a British wartime submachine gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alive and present in the world is the state of living.

clue.text: My twice-used letter opener?

indicators.note: twice-used says the piece appears two times in a row

parts.note: a letter traditionally opens with Dear

explanation.surface: Someone asks about a paper knife that has been used twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter opener' looks like a knife; it is the greeting that starts a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: My! is an exclamation of surprise or dismay, as is the doubled expression of mild alarm.

clue.text: Type of bread with pickle, good with some water

parts.note: a pickle is a tight spot, and so is a hole
rain is a quantity of water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: A sandwich order: bread with pickle, good with a glass of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pickle' suggests chutney in a sandwich; here it is a predicament, a HOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread made from unrefined flour keeping the whole kernel is a kind of loaf.

clue.text: Thinking old doctor will turn up to fix hip at home

indicators.note: the doctor's letters go round the two pieces, holding them in place
in a down answer turning up means reading the letters upward, backwards

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner
in means fashionable, hip
in means at home

explanation.surface: A retired doctor will show up to fix a patient's hip at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hip' looks like the joint; it means fashionable, IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding or expressing a view is a form of thinking or believing.

clue.text: Fish choking nets

indicators.note: the word choking nets, or catches, the fish within its letters

explanation.surface: A fish gets caught and chokes in the nets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nets' looks like fishing gear, but it is the verb saying 'choking' holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A New Zealand sea fish related to the hake, much used for fillets.

clue.text: Supervised deliveries? Bless!

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries
aw and bless are both cooing expressions of affection

explanation.surface: A midwife oversaw the deliveries, and everyone cooed over the babies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deliveries' suggests births; in cricket, overs are sets of six balls.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping watch over work being done is managing or directing it.

clue.text: Polish: spoken European language

indicators.note: spoken means the word is said out loud, giving a word that sounds alike

parts.note: Finnish is the language of Finland

explanation.surface: A list of European languages: Polish, spoken by many.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the language; it is the verb meaning to put a shine on.
explanation.definitionFit: A surface coating or sheen given to furniture is a final gloss.

clue.text: Plant, one found near river, secured by stake

indicators.note: the stake word holds the pair inside it, as a post secures something

parts.note: a stake is a bar or post driven into the ground

indicators.note: found near says the one letter sits right beside the river letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A plant growing by a river is tied to a stake to keep it upright.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorny shrub such as the wild rose, or the heath whose root makes pipes, is a plant.

clue.text: Former singer and blog writer, oddly

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of the words blog writer

explanation.surface: A singer from the past who has turned into a strange blogger.
explanation.definitionFit: David, the late British rock star of Ziggy Stardust fame, was a singer now gone.

clue.text: Wise caterers employed by Southbank theatre will?

indicators.note: employed by puts the caterers word alongside the theatre, as staff work for a venue

parts.note: caterers provide, or supply, food
the National Theatre, NT, stands on London's South Bank

explanation.surface: Caterers hired by a theatre on London's South Bank wonder whether they will be wise.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Theatre is a London theatre on the South Bank of the Thames; 'will?' asks what caterers will do, which is provide.
explanation.definitionFit: Being prudent and planning for the future is a form of wisdom.

clue.text: Experts on English translation exercise

indicators.note: in a down answer on means the experts word sits on top of the English letter

parts.note: pros are professionals, experts

explanation.surface: Professionals set a translation exercise for students of English.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage translated into a foreign language as a school exercise, as in Latin prose composition.

clue.text: Flower otherwise withers

indicators.note: withers suggests the word otherwise shrivels and loses its form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A flower would otherwise wither, a warning about care.
explanation.walkthrough: The flower is the emblem of Yorkshire, a county in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale rose bloom, emblem of the House of York, is a flower.

clue.text: Writer's current book dispatched without back cover

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: the back cover of a word is its last letter, which is removed

parts.note: something dispatched has been sent

explanation.surface: An author's latest book is sent off without its back cover.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian dramatist who wrote A Doll's House was a playwright, a writer.

clue.text: Prepare for attack from English forest, briefly

indicators.note: briefly means the forest name is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: Arden is the forest in Warwickshire, and in As You Like It

explanation.surface: Troops in an English forest get ready for an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: A fencer's call warning an opponent to take a guard position before a bout.

clue.text: Vintage red? We will imbibe one mouthful between meals?

parts.note: Che Guevara is a revolutionary of an earlier era, a red

indicators.note: the we word drinks in the one letter, taking it inside

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A wine buff asks if a vintage red will be sipped as a snack between meals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vintage red' suggests old wine; it is Che Guevara, an old revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for chewing gum, something to chew between meals, shown by the question mark as a loose example.
